{
  "items": [
    {
      "formal_name": "Int.sum_div",
      "informal_name": "Sum Division Equality for Divisible Terms in Integers",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {ι : Type u_5} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → ℤ} {n : ℤ}, (∀ i ∈ s, n ∣ f i) → (∑ i ∈ s, f i) / n = ∑ i ∈ s, f i / n",
      "informal_description": "For any finite set $ s $ and function $ f : s \\to \\mathbb{Z} $, if $ n $ divides each $ f(i) $ for all $ i \\in s $, then $ \\frac{1}{n} \\sum_{i \\in s} f(i) = \\sum_{i \\in s} \\frac{f(i)}{n} $.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Ring.Finset"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Nat.sum_div",
      "informal_name": "Distributivity of Division Over Sum for Divisible Terms",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ {ι : Type u_5} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → ℕ} {n : ℕ}, (∀ i ∈ s, n ∣ f i) → (∑ i ∈ s, f i) / n = ∑ i ∈ s, f i / n",
      "informal_description": "If $ n $ divides $ f(i) $ for all $ i $ in a finite set $ s $, then $ \\frac{1}{n} \\sum_{i \\in s} f(i) = \\sum_{i \\in s} \\frac{f(i)}{n} $. This holds for natural numbers under the condition that $ n $ divides each term $ f(i) $ in the sum.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Ring.Finset"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Rat.add_den_dvd",
      "informal_name": "Denominator of Sum Divides Product of Denominators for Rational Numbers",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ (q₁ q₂ : ℚ), (q₁ + q₂).den ∣ q₁.den * q₂.den",
      "informal_description": "For any rational numbers $q_1$ and $q_2$, the denominator of their sum $q_1 + q_2$ divides the product of their individual denominators, i.e., $\\mathrm{den}(q_1 + q_2) \\mid \\mathrm{den}(q_1) \\cdot \\mathrm{den}(q_2)$.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Data.Rat.Lemmas"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Rat.add_den_dvd_lcm",
      "informal_name": "Denominator of Sum Divides LCM of Denominators in Rational Numbers",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ (q₁ q₂ : ℚ), (q₁ + q₂).den ∣ q₁.den.lcm q₂.den",
      "informal_description": "For any two rational numbers $q_1$ and $q_2$, the denominator of their sum $q_1 + q_2$ divides the least common multiple of their individual denominators, i.e., $(q_1 + q_2).\\text{den} \\mid \\text{lcm}(q_1.\\text{den}, q_2.\\text{den})$.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Data.Rat.Lemmas"
    },
    {
      "formal_name": "Rat.sub_den_dvd",
      "informal_name": "Denominator of Rational Difference Divides Product of Denominators",
      "kind": "theorem",
      "type": "∀ (q₁ q₂ : ℚ), (q₁ - q₂).den ∣ q₁.den * q₂.den",
      "informal_description": "For any rational numbers $ q_1 $ and $ q_2 $, the denominator of $ q_1 - q_2 $ divides the product of the denominators of $ q_1 $ and $ q_2 $, i.e., $ \\operatorname{den}(q_1 - q_2) \\mid \\operatorname{den}(q_1) \\cdot \\operatorname{den}(q_2) $.",
      "path": "Mathlib.Data.Rat.Lemmas"
    }
  ]
}

items.informal_name: Sum Division Equality for Divisible Terms in Integers
items.type: ∀ {ι : Type u_5} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → ℤ} {n : ℤ}, (∀ i ∈ s, n ∣ f i) → (∑ i ∈ s, f i) / n = ∑ i ∈ s, f i / n
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $ and function $ f : s \to \mathbb{Z} $, if $ n $ divides each $ f(i) $ for all $ i \in s $, then $ \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i \in s} f(i) = \sum_{i \in s} \frac{f(i)}{n} $.

items.informal_name: Distributivity of Division Over Sum for Divisible Terms
items.type: ∀ {ι : Type u_5} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → ℕ} {n : ℕ}, (∀ i ∈ s, n ∣ f i) → (∑ i ∈ s, f i) / n = ∑ i ∈ s, f i / n
items.informal_description: If $ n $ divides $ f(i) $ for all $ i $ in a finite set $ s $, then $ \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i \in s} f(i) = \sum_{i \in s} \frac{f(i)}{n} $. This holds for natural numbers under the condition that $ n $ divides each term $ f(i) $ in the sum.

items.informal_name: Denominator of Sum Divides Product of Denominators for Rational Numbers
items.informal_description: For any rational numbers $q_1$ and $q_2$, the denominator of their sum $q_1 + q_2$ divides the product of their individual denominators, i.e., $\mathrm{den}(q_1 + q_2) \mid \mathrm{den}(q_1) \cdot \mathrm{den}(q_2)$.

items.informal_name: Denominator of Sum Divides LCM of Denominators in Rational Numbers
items.informal_description: For any two rational numbers $q_1$ and $q_2$, the denominator of their sum $q_1 + q_2$ divides the least common multiple of their individual denominators, i.e., $(q_1 + q_2).\text{den} \mid \text{lcm}(q_1.\text{den}, q_2.\text{den})$.

items.informal_name: Denominator of Rational Difference Divides Product of Denominators
items.informal_description: For any rational numbers $ q_1 $ and $ q_2 $, the denominator of $ q_1 - q_2 $ divides the product of the denominators of $ q_1 $ and $ q_2 $, i.e., $ \operatorname{den}(q_1 - q_2) \mid \operatorname{den}(q_1) \cdot \operatorname{den}(q_2) $.
